clue.text: State of panic in apartment with fast turnaround?

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, the British word for it
a spin is a quick rotation, a turning round at speed

explanation.surface: Someone panics about their flat after a hurried rotation of tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'fast turnaround' is a playful description of a spin rather than a business term.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in a tizzy of confusion and alarm is being in a flat spin, from aircraft going out of control.

clue.text: Detest swear-word appearing in French article

indicators.note: appearing in places the swear-word inside the French article

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
an oath is a curse or swear-word

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a rude word turning up in a French magazine piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detest something is to hate it intensely.

clue.text: Outdo last in tournament, bottom

indicators.note: last in asks for the final letter of the word tournament

parts.note: the rump is the backside or bottom

explanation.surface: A player finishing last in a tournament ends up at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' and 'bottom' paint a losing player, the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to trump someone is to beat or surpass them, as a trump card beats others.

clue.text: Tested about Latin language

parts.note: something tested and shown true is proven
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone's knowledge of Latin was put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Romance tongue of Provence in southern France, also called Occitan.

clue.text: One coming from Las Vegas, perhaps in van Dean ordered

definitions.text: One coming from Las Vegas, perhaps

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of van and Dean are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Dean drives a van, maybe arriving from Las Vegas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Las Vegas is a city in the US state of Nevada, so its residents are natives of that state.

clue.text: Powerful male, heavy, we dropped

indicators.note: dropped says the word we is taken out of the synonym for heavy

parts.note: weighty means heavy

explanation.surface: A strong, heavy man got dropped by our team.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mighty means having great strength or force.

clue.text: Month in America, below zero

parts.note: US, the United States, stands for America

explanation.surface: A month spent in America with temperatures beneath freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative number or temperature lies under nought, written with a minus sign.

clue.text: High-octane event in which farceur falls under £1,000 piano

indicators.note: in a down entry, falls under puts the farceur's name below the other pieces

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
Brian Rix was a famous British actor of Whitehall farces

explanation.surface: At some event an actor topples beneath a piano costing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian Rix was a British comic actor famous for stage farces. 'Falls under' is the positional signal, putting RIX beneath GRAND and P.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Formula One race is a fast, fuel-burning motor sport occasion, literally high-octane.

clue.text: Going off after short time harness racing

indicators.note: after puts the decaying word behind the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
food going off is rotting

explanation.surface: Something spoiling after a brief interval at a horse track.
explanation.definitionFit: Harness racing is the sport of horses pulling sulkies at a trot, so it is also called trotting.

clue.text: Opera singer's brief song about us

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the opera singer is the answer

indicators.note: about means the shortened song goes round us
brief means the song's word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a carol is a song, especially at Christmas
taken as written

explanation.surface: An opera singer's short song is about the people singing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' and 'about' look like they describe the song, but they are the trimming and wrapping signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Enrico Caruso was the great Italian tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: French wine old boy brought back — ring for a curry

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: brought back says the old boy pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Wine from France, an old boy returning, and a phone call ordering a takeaway curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' reverses O plus LAD to give DALO. 'Old boy' looks like one unit (OB), but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: vindaloo is a fiery Indian-restaurant dish of Goan origin.

clue.text: Guide female lead in play, and her daughter

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: lead in asks for the opening letter of the word play

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman takes the lead role in a play, alongside her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a starring role, but it picks the first letter of 'play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to shepherd people is to guide or herd them along, as a sheep farmer drives a flock.

clue.text: Composed? Some composed, at ease

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is a calm person one who is relaxed and at ease?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone calm and unhurried is sedate, in the adjective sense of composure.

clue.text: Alternative choice in back row

parts.note: to second a motion is to back or support it
a string is a row or line of things

explanation.surface: An understudy waits in the back row as the fallback option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In back row' reads as a location in a theatre or team photo; 'back' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a reserve player or backup option is a second-string choice.

clue.text: Triumph or one will take your place

parts.note: success is a triumph
taken as written

explanation.surface: Either you triumph or someone replaces you.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who follows another into a job or title is the one who replaces them.

clue.text: Advance point of view in matter

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money against wages
a stance is a position or viewpoint

explanation.surface: Someone moves a viewpoint forward in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: physical matter or material is called substance.

clue.text: Severely scold model turning up to disrupt hunt

indicators.note: to disrupt means the model piece breaks into the word for hunt

parts.note: to chase is to hunt

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word for model is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone sharply rebukes a fashion model who arrives to ruin a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a catwalk, but here it is the verb for posing for an artist; 'turning up' works upwards because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to chastise is to reprimand harshly or punish.

clue.text: Ever so pretty externally, its contents may be plain

definitions.text: Ever so pretty externally, its contents may be plain

parts.words: Ever so pretty externally, its contents may be plain
parts.note: a sweets carton has a sweetly pretty picture on its lid, and inside may be plain (dark) confectionery; the phrase also describes a twee, picture-postcard look

explanation.surface: Something gorgeous on the outside may be ordinary within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like the opposite of pretty, but it means dark, as in plain cocoa sweets rather than milk ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a crossword-style double sense: a sweets carton, and an adjective for twee, chocolate-pretty scenery.

clue.text: Large tank erected near badly prepared restaurant

indicators.note: in a down entry, erected means the tank word is stood upright, read upwards

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids

indicators.note: badly prepared means the letters of near are mixed up

explanation.surface: A big tank is set up beside a poorly run eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' turns VAT into TAV; 'badly prepared' scrambles NEAR into ERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Greek eatery or café is called a taverna.

clue.text: Reportedly up against a brick wall, old plaster

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for that predicament is heard rather than seen

parts.note: someone up against a brick wall can go no further: they are stuck

explanation.surface: Someone stuck against a brick wall covered in old plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster or render used to coat walls and mouldings.

clue.text: Gathers European rejected honour

indicators.note: rejected means both preceding pieces are turned back

parts.note: people who gather meet, so gathers means meets

explanation.surface: A European is rejected for an honour at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns back MEETS plus E together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to esteem someone is to respect and hold them in high regard.

clue.text: A myth, terrible nonsense

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of a myth are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A myth is just awful rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the exclamation dismisses something as rubbish, like saying 'nonsense!'.

clue.text: Very with it in Mediterranean country, so go

indicators.note: in puts it inside the country's name

parts.note: Italy is a Mediterranean country
taken as written

explanation.surface: Very trendy in Italy, so off you go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' looks like 'trendy', but 'with' is only a joining word and IT is taken as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: go in the noun sense of energy and drive, as in 'full of go'.

clue.text: Louts vandalised plant

indicators.note: vandalised means the letters of louts are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Hooligans trashed a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lotus is a water lily, an aquatic flowering plant.

clue.text: Princes bemused about hot dog

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the letter for hot
bemused means the letters of princes are confused

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Royal princes puzzled over a hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as one snack; 'hot' gives H and 'dog' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Doberman pinscher and miniature pinscher are German dog breeds.

clue.text: Become aware of warning

definitions.meaning: an advance notification, as in a week's ... or a warning posted up

explanation.surface: Realising there is an alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to observe something, and a formal alert or notification given in advance.

clue.text: Assiduous searcher, bishop in the company of walkers

indicators.note: in the company of puts the bishop's letters among the walkers, inside them

parts.note: feet are what we walk with
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A diligent investigator is a bishop who joins a party of ramblers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walkers' looks like hikers, but it means the body parts we walk on; Right Reverend is a bishop's formal title.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a person who rummages persistently is called this, after the burrowing polecat used for hunting rabbits.

clue.text: Dislike a Biblical translation

parts.note: a version is a translation, as in the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a particular rendering of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aversion is a strong distaste or dislike, noun for noun.
